In recent weeks, ChatGPT users were only subject to a weekly usage cap, but OpenAI announced today (the 25th) that the five-hour usage limit for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work will be reinstated. Details are as follows.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers will see the five-hour usage cap reinstated

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, head of engineering for OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT, announced tonight (the 25th) that starting tomorrow (the 26th), the five-hour usage limit for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work will be reinstated.

Once users hit the five-hour or weekly cap, they can wait for the next cycle to reset, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also occasionally reset users' usage for free; users can earn stored reset quotas through designated promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, in recent weeks, OpenAI had temporarily removed the five-hour usage limit on Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly cap.

During that period, the company also reset users' weekly allowances ahead of schedule several times to celebrate milestones, including reaching one million additional active users across these two (now-merged) platforms combined.

But as Tibo explained on X tonight (the 25th):

"Tomorrow we will reinstate the five-hour limit for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex. I mentioned this before, then postponed it. We need to do this because (1) the five-hour limit helps us spread the compute load and keep the weekly allowance more generous; (2) most Plus plan users are relatively light, new users who sometimes unconsciously burn through an entire week's quota and then feel confused — not a great experience. Over the coming months, the $100 and $200 Pro subscriptions will continue to have no five-hour limit."

Tibo did not mention any changes for Enterprise or Education accounts, which currently use a separate credit-based usage system.

Does the reinstatement of the five-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
